How this book matches your exam. This book is checked against the Cambridge 0452 syllabus for 2027, 2028 and 2029. The syllabus has seven topics:

  1. Fundamentals of accounting
  2. Sources and recording of data
  3. Verification of accounting records
  4. Accounting procedures
  5. Preparation of financial statements
  6. Analysis and interpretation
  7. Accounting concepts and modern practice (including ethics, technology and sustainability, which are new)

Papers:

  • Paper 1: multiple choice, 40 questions, 1 h 30 min, 30%.
  • Paper 2: structured written paper, 5 compulsory questions, 100 marks, 1 h 45 min, 70%.

Assessment objectives: knowledge and understanding 66%, analysis 24%, evaluation 10%.

2026 exams use the previous syllabus, and the accounting methods are the same. This book covers Topic 1 (1.1 The purpose of accounting; 1.2 The accounting equation). Every figure was checked by computer, and every equation balances. The marking guides are our own, not official Cambridge mark schemes.

Unit 1 of 10: The Purpose of Accounting

Key ideas

  • Accounting records, summarises and reports financial information so that people can make decisions.
  • Purposes:
  • record transactions;
  • calculate profit or loss;
  • show the financial position (assets and liabilities);
  • help with control (e.g. of cash, inventory and amounts owed);
  • help with planning and decision-making;
  • meet legal requirements (tax).

Worked examples

Example 1: a shop owner checks the year's profit to decide whether to open a second branch.

Example 2: records of money owed by customers help the business chase late payers.

Example 3: the tax authority needs accurate profit figures.

10-mark exam-style question

(a) State three purposes of accounting. [3] (b) Explain how accounting records help a business owner control the business. [3] (c) Explain why a business owner needs to know the profit or loss. [4]

Answers: (a) Record transactions; calculate profit or loss; show the financial position (or help decisions, control, meet legal requirements) (B3). (b) Records show what is owed by customers (B1), so overdue amounts can be chased (B1); inventory records help prevent theft or waste (B1). (c) To judge whether the business is successful (B1); to decide on drawings / expansion (B1); to calculate tax (B1); to show lenders that the business can repay loans (B1).

Common mistakes

  1. Saying the purpose is "to count money". 2. Confusing control with planning. 3. Vague answers. 4. Ignoring legal requirements. 5. Not developing the points.

Quick recall

  1. A purpose of accounting? 2. Profit shows? 3. What does the statement of financial position show? 4. Why do tax authorities need accounts? 5. Control example?

Answers: 1) Recording transactions. 2) Success or failure over a period. 3) Assets and liabilities at a date. 4) To calculate tax. 5) Chasing amounts owed by customers.
